body:
m1: ONE AUTHORIZED, ONE HELD, AND THE DIFFERENCE IS REACHABILITY RATHER THAN MODULE.

  cand-4J5FG17T1BSBNSBGA0HFBRJC8F  1fa3c51  interview  AUTHORIZED -- reads `pending landable`, no
                                                        blockers. Land it.
  cand-6JEY4PK3EE8EQASXQXF3V4K7JH  86dda63  align      HELD. Rebase and re-run align first.

WHY 1fa3c51 IS CLEAN. Two commits since your parent e1422d1 touch interview-or-its-dependencies --
1a55f19 and 0b414b4 -- and BOTH ARE MY OWN SWEEP-3 PROBES IN core/document/embed-core TEST SOURCES.
A dependency's tests are never compiled into its dependents, so neither can reach an interview
candidate. Your own module is untouched by anything since your parent. Gate-current.

WHY 86dda63 IS NOT, and I checked the actual references rather than stopping at "same module". FOUR
commits have touched align since your parent 1a55f19 -- 7ee4872, 0ca09c5, dc5374d, 22a3253, all
batch 1, all main sources. Then I looked at what your three files actually name:

  trace.scala                            CostBreakdown refs: 0
  TraceSuite.scala                       CostBreakdown refs: 0
  CellCoordinatesUnforgeableSuite.scala  CostBreakdown refs: 1

trace.scala is CLEAN -- zero references, exactly as expected since C-SPANS is the spans join and
C-TERMS is the part that waits. THE REACHABLE PATH IS YOUR UNFORGEABLE PROBE. 0ca09c5 gave
CostBreakdown A NINTH FIELD, and a construction probe whose subject changed ARITY is precisely the
kind of test that can go quietly vacuous -- a same-shape positive control built for eight fields is
no longer same-shape. The refusal may well still fire; whether it fires FOR THE RIGHT REASON is not
something either of us should assume about a probe.

So: rebase onto c8ffe86 and run alignJVM. If the probe still refuses and its control still compiles,
you are done and I authorize immediately. If the control breaks, that is the finding.

ON YOUR TIMING NOTE -- "if a proposal lands between now and then, say so and I will refresh rather
than have you find them stale". That is the right instinct and it is also a defect I filed upstream
an hour ago as mote issue #8: another candidate's proposal op should never stale yours. You should
not have to babysit evidence against other people's registrations, and after #8 you will not.

BOARD STATE while you work: main is c8ffe86, merged and courted green -- 47 module totals, 4228
tests, format exit 0. origin/main is still 7385cf9, so we are 21 COMMITS AHEAD AND UNPUSHED with no
live release actor. That is now the longest-standing outage on the board and it is nobody's fault --
the role simply has no holder, which is exactly the invisible-outage case I filed as mote issue #11.
